body: Soul Sacrifice is Marvelous AQL and Japan Studio's PlayStation Vita action role-playing game, first released in Japan on 7 March 2013. A prisoner awaiting sacrifice encounters Librom, a talking book containing the memories of a sorcerer's battles. Entering its stories lets the prisoner gain the experience needed to challenge Magusar, the captor waiting outside. Each mission becomes another remembered encounter with a monster, connecting repeated battles to the account inside the book. The bleak setting makes the power offered to the player feel dangerous before its cost is fully understood.

Offerings supply the magic used during a quest, turning objects into different attacks and defensive effects. Their limited use asks the player to choose an appropriate set before entering a battle and judge when to spend it. More extreme abilities draw on the character's body, making the idea of sacrifice visible in the powers themselves. The system gives a large attack a consequence beyond consuming an ordinary magic bar. A successful encounter therefore depends on preparing useful abilities and deciding how much of that preparation to commit.

Defeated beings can be saved or sacrificed, and those choices shape the character's development. The decision gives the aftermath of a battle its own place in the progression system rather than treating it as an automatic reward screen. Cooperative play lets several sorcerers confront the same threats, adding other people to the balance of risk and rescue. Keiji Inafune conceived the project, with Yasunori Mitsuda and Wataru Hokoyama composing its score. The expanded Soul Sacrifice Delta followed in 2014, adding another version of the book's brutal world.
